message.content: I researched Apple's latest results and news, then bought 40 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.70 (filled at $222.70, ~$8,908 total, within the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, funded from existing $50,000 cash with no money moved out). Apple's fiscal Q4 2024 (quarter ended Sept 28, 2024) showed revenue of $94.9B, up 6% year over year, and full fiscal 2024 net sales of $391.0B with net income of $93.7B, or $6.08 diluted EPS — figures confirmed in the 10-K filed Nov 1, 2024 (revenue $391,035M, net income $93,736M, diluted EPS $6.08), noting the year included a one-time $10.2B tax charge. News flow was neutral-to-constructive: shares were steady around $222 as investors weighed iPhone 16 demand and the gradual Apple Intelligence rollout, and the quote ($222.70 last, $222.68/$222.72 bid-ask) put my limit essentially at market. I sized the order modestly given the neutral near-term sentiment and the fact that the strong annual figures were partly flattered by services growth while hardware demand remains an open question.
